boundaries.description: The bottom of the framework: pure domain types, branded ids and discriminated unions. Imports nothing upward; the one shared/ edge is the public barrel re-exporting the pure JSON-patch impl.
Pure utilities (topo sort, hashing, JSON patch, composite node-address codec). Depends on types/ and the logger seam only; never on the runtime or a backend.
The generic state-machine kernel: transitions, replay, serialization. Pure over types/; knows no DAG, no backend and no transport.

Pure transitions plus the imperative execution shell for one DAG run. May read the runtime's own collaborators (tracing, logger, observer, queue, checkpoint, the eval-judge node types) but never the public executor, the LLM clients, the caches or a transport adapter.
The cron scheduler: a timer-driven shell over the queue port and the logger. No transport adapter, no host.
The BullMQ/Redis queue adapter. Owns the only sanctioned bullmq + ioredis imports outside the redis checkpoint/cache adapters; may use the executor in tests.

The framework package root: everything not claimed by a finer boundary (executor, llm, nodes, cache, checkpoint, file, observer, tracing, cli, scripts). Imports its own tree plus declared externals; never the host package (except the generated-app contract in codegen/docs) or an adapter package.
The host's functional core: pure state machines, config parsing, error mapping, auth model. Imports ports and the framework only; never an adapter, the HTTP shell or the lifecycle shell.
The git sync loop: timer-driven shell over the registry and the git adapter. Reads the domain and its ports; never the HTTP shell or the top-level wiring.
The HTTP shell: Hono routes, handlers and middleware. Orchestrates the domain, the ports, the supervisor, the HITL service and the adapters it is wired with; never the top-level host wiring.
Boot, signals and the Redis probe: the process-lifecycle shell. Domain, ports, adapters and sync; never the HTTP shell or top-level wiring.

The host's infrastructure adapters (Redis, git, Graph, Keycloak, spend authority, run executor). Implements domain-owned ports; may read the domain, the ports and the sibling shells it adapts, never the top-level wiring.

The host package root: the top-level shell (host.ts, main.ts), the supervisor, the HITL subsystem, entrypoint wiring and the ports module. Composes everything inside the package; never reaches into framework internals or another package's source.
CockroachDB/Postgres capability adapter. Depends on the framework's adapter-factory surface and its own driver.
Oracle capability adapter. Depends on the framework's adapter-factory surface and the injected driver.
Microsoft Graph document capability adapter. Depends on the framework and the document-source port; never the host.
Shared HTTP auth primitives (JWKS verification, claims policy). Depends on the framework's Result surface; never the host.
The document-source port and its shared types. Framework Result surface only.
The streaming XLSX reader and its benches: own tree plus node built-ins, its two runtime deps, and the dev-only differential oracles (xlsx/exceljs/jszip) which only tests and benches may use.
The local-filesystem document-source adapter: framework Result surface plus node:fs.
Runnable example DAGs: the public framework surface, the document-source port, and the host's registration contract — never host internals.
The customer-summary deployable: composes the public framework surface and the host contract with its own SDK and telemetry deps; never reaches into another workspace's source.
The human-in-the-loop smoke example: public framework surface and the host registration contract only.
Repo tooling and connectivity smokes: may drive any workspace package (including its source, to smoke one adapter in isolation); nothing imports scripts/.

impureModules.reason: systemClock — the one wall-clock read inside types/; every other module in types/ is pure
node:crypto's synchronous HMAC/timingSafeEqual primitives — pure computation over its inputs, but the purity rule's node: predicate cannot distinguish a primitive from I/O
lifecycle connect/close orchestration: it drives async handle connects and reports failed-cleanup diagnostics through an injected sink (the pure helpers it calls stay pure)
races a promise against a timer: the timer is the one I/O this module exists to perform, and the caller needs the settlement to fire before an outer deadline rather than to compute anything
